corrections.reason: The stored -33.57 (first-author upload c810bdc, 2022-07-16: -33.57 | 0.01 | 0.80(3), never changed) is -0.5245313 per site, outside the printed cell -0.5244 under either reading: 0.3 of a last-digit unit beyond the truncation window (-0.5245, -0.5244] and 0.8 beyond the rounding window [-0.52445, -0.52435). The paper prints -0.5244(6) in both the journal SI and arXiv v2. It is the only stored cell of SI Tables 4 and 5 that reproduces its printed digits under neither reading (every other one does under at least one: 4 x 16 PBC-OBC under rounding only, 8 x 8 U = 4 under truncation only, 6 x 6 U = 8 under truncation and on a rounding tie, the other six under both). SI Fig. 4 (vector marks re-read 2026-09-29) plots the point at relative error 2.839e-3 against AFQMC -33.66, i.e. -0.524444 per site = -33.5644 total: inside the printed cell and 0.0056 above the upload. The figure is not exact at this level (its 6 x 6 U = 8 point, -18.9761, sits 0.0023 below that upload and outside its own printed cell), and the upload's two decimals leave one reconciliation open (a raw total in (-33.568, -33.565) rounds to -33.57 and truncates to -0.5244), so this replaces a coarser upload by the printed value rather than repairing a proven slip. The correction raises the energy by 0.0084 (0.22 printed sigma, 0.84 upload sigma); the row stays the instance's only variational row, 0.098 above the sign-free AFQMC -33.66(2), so no record changes; v_score is derived and follows. Everything else checks: 8 x 8 PA, 32 + 32, U = 8, N~ = 16, alpha = 1 (SI Sec. 6), variational, own computation, PNAS; no duplicate on the instance. The finding text of the existing defect on square_64_PA_32_6 lists -33.57 among the uploads that 'match the paper'; that sentence should be amended if this is accepted.

compute.reported_as: We typically choose tau = 0.01 in this work, with which we have verified that the Trotter error is below the targeted statistical errors. || In this section, we present results at half-filling. As mentioned, the AFQMC results are numerically exact, as the sign problem is absent because of the particle-hole symmetry. We use a combination of the path-integral approach [40] and the random walk approach [25]. || In this work, we use a special form of the generalized Hartree-Fock (GHF) [34] wave function as TWF in the AFQMC calculations. This will increase the computation time by a factor of 2 to 4 in different portions of algorithm, because now the Slater determinant of up and down spin are coupled. || Earlier calculations were carried out at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Most of the calculations were carried out at the Extreme Science and Engineering Discovery Environment (XSEDE), which is supported by National Science Foundation Grant No. ACI-1053575, and the computational facilities at the College of William and Mary.
compute.source: Sec. II B (Trotter step); Sec. IV Results at half filling; Sec. III B (GHF trial wave function); Acknowledgments; energies from Appendix Table IV, arXiv:1605.09421 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Half-filling AFQMC data of Appendix Table IV (PBC and PBC-APBC, 4x4 to 16x16, U = 2-8). No walker counts, projection times, sample/block counts, core counts, core-hours or wall-clock are stated anywhere for these runs; the only quantitative method setting is the Trotter step tau = 0.01 (with a tau -> 0 extrapolation used only for the TABC data). The GHF trial-wave-function remark is a relative cost (factor 2-4 in computation time), not an absolute one.
